result.message: Current game resource index. Inventory array indices are object IDs; startingRoom is the initial location.

Walking, barriers, triggers and water

Every step of every object is judged against the control priorities under its baseline, the cel-wide row of pixels at its feet. The interpreters scan that row left to right:

- Control 0 blocks. Control 1 blocks unless ignore.blocks. Control 2 is a trigger: f3 is set for ego when ANY baseline pixel touches control 2, so a one-pixel-wide trigger line is enough and ego cannot stand across it without triggering. Control 3 is water: f0 is set only when EVERY baseline pixel is on water, so a shoreline reads as land until the whole footprint is in. obj.on.water and obj.on.land gate movement with that all-cells rule.
- Priority 15 objects skip the scan entirely and clear both flags. Fixed priority does not skip it.
- Paint barriers along the visible obstacle they represent and leave exits open; a stray control-0 pixel in a doorway is the most common walking bug. A priority fill floods the connected region, so close every outline before filling. Keep open floor at 4.
- Room edges: ego touching an edge sets v2 (1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 left) for one cycle; the room logic reads it and calls new.room. set.horizon(y) keeps ego below the sky line unless ignore.horizon.
- Scripted movement: move.obj(o, x, y, step, f) walks an object to a point and sets f on arrival. On ego it takes control away from the player until arrival or a border stop, then hands it back and zeroes v6. A zero-distance move.obj on ego is the idiom for handing control back after a scripted placement. program.control and player.control switch it explicitly; wander(o) and follow.ego(o, distance, f) are the other motions.
- reposition(o, dx, dy) moves an object by variable deltas and runs the placement check at once, so a script can slide ego along a trigger line and wait for the exact pixel where a flag fires. The Gold Rush demonstration does exactly that to reach one coordinate.
- Death and failure: when the player walks into danger, decide it from the control screen or a posn() box, print a short message with a wry line, and offer restore. Keep the dangerous area visibly different so the death is fair.

rooms.title: The Castle Gate
rooms.description: Opening room. Wenna stands on the meadow before Thornwall's gray gate. A royal notice on a post (taking it accepts the errand), a covered basket holding bread, and a lit brass lantern on a hook. An alligator watches from the moat; swimming earns a warning, then death. The drawbridge leads north into the hall; the path runs east to the meadow.

rooms.title: Meadow Crossroads
rooms.description: Open meadow where the paths meet, with a signpost and the first unlit roadside candle (light it with the lantern). Paths west to the castle, north to the old oak, east to the river gorge, south to the stove hut.

rooms.title: River Gorge
rooms.description: A blue river cuts into a gorge. A heron on a rock wants to discuss the bread first; give it bread and it shows the stepping stones down the river (+20). At the bottom, the Bell lies underwater; Wenna recovers it (+40). Second roadside candle on the bank.

rooms.title: The Stove Hut
rooms.description: A crooked hut with smoke from a crooked chimney. Inside the stove lives a vain salamander that guards the undying Ember. It is easily impressed by polished brass: polish the brass lantern (with Wenna's oversized sleeve) and show it, and it trades the Ember, which rides in the lantern (+40).

rooms.title: The Old Oak and the Talking Well
rooms.description: An old woman knits with map-thread under a great oak beside a talking well. She asks a riddle; wrong answers earn hints, and the well offers clues. The right answer earns the wandering Map (+40). Third roadside candle by the well.

rooms.title: The Great Hall
rooms.description: King Brannoc waits beside the kingdom's last burning candle. He is tired, funny and determined. He comments on the errand; bringing the Bell, Ember and Map restores Thornwall (+60) and ends the story, with a remark if all three roadside candles are lit.

exits.name: south across the drawbridge to the gate

facts.name: protagonist
facts.text: Wenna, third squire to King Brannoc of Thornwall. Short brown hair, rust-red tunic, sleeves too big. Ego view 0.

facts.name: goal
facts.text: Recover the Three Bright Things (Bell, Ember, Map) and bring them to King Brannoc in the hall (room 6) before the last candle burns out. The candle is urgency flavor only; there is no timer death.

facts.name: inventory
facts.text: Object IDs: 0 '?' placeholder, 1 royal notice, 2 bread, 3 brass lantern (lit), 4 Bell, 5 Ember, 6 Map. Items 1-3 start in room 1; 4-6 start inactive and are given by logic.

facts.name: score
facts.text: Max 230 in v7. 10 accept errand (take notice, room 1, f32). 20 help heron (room 3, f37). 40 Bell (f38). 40 Ember (f39). 40 Map (f40). 60 restore Thornwall (room 6, f44). 20 when all three roadside candles are lit (f41 meadow, f42 river, f43 oak; v32 counts lit candles; award at v32==3).

facts.name: candles
facts.text: Three roadside candles: meadow (room 2), river (room 3), oak (room 5). 'light candle' needs the lantern (item 3). Increment v32 per candle; when it reaches 3 add 20 points once.

facts.name: deaths
facts.text: Swimming in the moat (room 1): first attempt warns (f35), second is eaten by the alligator and calls logic 255. Wrong answers elsewhere earn hints, never death. Treasures cannot be lost.

facts.name: brass
facts.text: The lantern is brass. The salamander admires polished brass; 'polish lantern' (with Wenna's sleeve) sets up the Ember trade in room 4.

facts.name: views
facts.text: View 0 Wenna (loops right,left,front,back). View 1 gate props (loop0 notice, loop1 basket cel0 covered/cel1 bread/cel2 empty, loop2 lantern flicker). View 2 alligator in the moat.
